title: CSS Advanced Concepts - Module #11578
question: What does the `will-change` CSS property do, and when should it be used?
options: It prevents CSS inheritance from parent layout containers.
It allows developers to write media queries inside styles dynamically.
It forces immediate layout re-calculations on all class `SessionTracker` instances.
It hints to the browser's rendering engine that an element will animate, letting it pre-render layer composites, but should be used sparingly.
answer: It hints to the browser's rendering engine that an element will animate, letting it pre-render layer composites, but should be used sparingly.
explanation: `will-change` sets up GPU acceleration layers before changes occur. Overusing it can consume too much memory and degrade performance.
